name: Rosenborg Castle
blurb: Renaissance royal castle ringed by a moat, now a museum of Denmark's royal treasures.
priceText: 150 kr (140 kr online), students 100 kr, free for under 17

name: National Museum of Denmark (Nationalmuseet)
blurb: Denmark's national history museum; many rank it among Europe's finest, with a well-organised permanent display.
priceText: 150 kr adult, 135 kr online, under 18 free

name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
blurb: Over 10,000 works spanning Egyptian, Greek and Roman antiquities through to Romantic art; cheap for under-27s.
priceText: Adult 115 kr, under 27 85 kr, under 18 and Tuesdays free

name: David Collection (Davids Samling)
blurb: Free entry to Islamic, 18th-century European and early Danish art; guided tours are in Danish, spring and autumn only.

name: Mio
blurb: Small takeaway pizza counter with cheap, medium-sized pies; you can carry them to the bar next door.
priceText: Veg pizza 49 kr, meat 59 kr, dessert 21 kr

name: Hansens Old Family Garden
blurb: Oldest of Frederiksberg's garden restaurants, its main building dating from 1630; classic Danish fare indoors or in the garden.

name: Dupong
blurb: Table-tennis and table-football bar: pay for a bat that includes a drink, play all night, then head downstairs for a proper bar.
priceText: 35 kr bat rental, includes one drink; water free

name: Culture Box
blurb: Electronic club that pairs star DJs with local talent; the crowd is friendly and open.

name: Copenhill
blurb: Ski and hike on the rooftop slope of a city incineration plant; the rooftop bar is free to visit.
priceText: 150 kr per hour for skiing; rooftop bar access free

name: Dyrehaven (The Deer Park)
blurb: Forest park of roughly 11 km² north of town, with a small royal hunting castle on a hilltop.

name: Vasa Museum
blurb: Museum around a 1628 warship that sank on its maiden voyage, salvaged in 1961 and now displayed almost whole.

name: Royal Palace (Kungliga Slottet)
blurb: Swedish royal residence built 1697–1754 at the north-east edge of the Old Town.
priceText: Adults 160 kr, students and children 80 kr

name: Nationalmuseum (National Museum of Fine Arts)
blurb: Sweden's national art museum with works by Rembrandt, Rubens, Goya and Degas; free on Thursday evenings.
priceText: 160 kr adult; free under 20; free Thursdays 17:00–20:00
when: Tue–Wed, Fri–Sun 11:00–17:00; Thu to 20:00; closed Mon

name: Storkyrkan (Stockholm Cathedral)
blurb: Gamla stan's oldest church: a 13th-century Gothic core with a Baroque face from about 1740; free to enter outside summer.
priceText: Entrance 40 kr 21 May–29 Sep; free rest of year

name: Pepe Nero
blurb: Hybrid of fast food and sit-down restaurant: mostly Italian plates, huge portions, and nearly every meal costs 95 kr.
priceText: Virtually every meal 95 kr; free water

name: Vete-Katten
blurb: Long-running café from 1928 with period interiors; cinnamon buns all year, saffron buns in November–December.

name: Dovas
blurb: Budget local bar on Kungsholmen with 500 ml ales around 30 kr; a nightclub across the road draws the crowd later.
priceText: 30 kr for a 500 ml bottle of Norrlands Guld or another local ale

name: Stampen
blurb: Gamla stan jazz venue dating from 1965, with live acts on most nights.

name: Storkyrkobadet
blurb: Hidden pool and sauna in a former Old Town wine cellar, bathing beneath 1700s vaults; men and women go on separate days.
priceText: Adults 40 kr incl. pool and sauna; students and seniors 30 kr
when: Men Tue, Fri, Sun; women Mon, Thu; 05:00–20:30; closed in summer

name: Old Town free walking tour (Stockholm Free Tour)
blurb: Daily free walking tour of Gamla stan that runs on donations; a handy way to get your bearings.

name: Röhsska Museum
blurb: Sweden's go-to museum for design and applied arts, with fixed and rotating shows; free if you're under 25.
priceText: Adult 60 kr (source reads 'or'), under 25 or Gothenburg Pass free
when: Tue–Wed 11:00–18:00; Thu to 20:00; Fri–Sun 11:00–17:00; closed 24 and 25 Dec, 31 Dec, 1 Jan

name: Gothenburg Art Museum (Göteborgs Konstmuseum)
blurb: Gothenburg's art museum, set in a stately building next to the theatre; its strength is Nordic art.
priceText: 60 kr; up to 20 and students with ID free

name: Haga district
blurb: One of the city's prettiest districts, with wooden houses from the 1800s; the bohemian Långgatan streets are close by.

name: Skanskaskrapan (Lipstick viewing platform)
blurb: Nicknamed 'the lipstick', this tower's viewing platform sits at 86 m; outside summer it opens on weekdays only.

name: Gothenburg Botanical Gardens
blurb: 175-hectare botanical garden with a rock garden, arboretum and greenhouses; entry is free except for the greenhouses.
priceText: Free entrance, except for the greenhouse

name: GöteborgsOperan behind-the-scenes tour
blurb: Gothenburg's modern opera house at Lilla Bommen, with guided backstage tours that explain how shows come together.

name: Gourmetkorv
blurb: Sausage specialist with 13 varieties, each served with potato salad or mash; cheap and filling.

name: Feskekörka (fish market hall)
blurb: Historic fish market hall that reopened after a major renovation; only a few restaurants and shops remain.

name: King's Head
blurb: Calmer, classier pub on a street better known for budget bars.

name: Nefertiti
blurb: Gothenburg nightclub playing house, jazz and northern soul.

name: Helsinki Lutheran Cathedral
blurb: White neoclassical cathedral on Senate Square, finished 1852; free to enter November–May (8 € voluntary fee).
priceText: Nov–May free (8 € voluntary fee); Jun–Aug 10 €, Sep–Oct 8 €

name: Temppeliaukio Church (Church in the Rock)
blurb: Church carved from bedrock, its roof made of around 22 km of copper strips; open daily, though services can close it.

name: Amos Rex
blurb: Contemporary art museum leaning toward immersive, often audiovisual works; entry is through Lasipalatsi.
priceText: General admission 22 € at the museum, 20 € online; students and 18–29 year olds 5 €

name: Helsinki City Museum
blurb: Free museum built around a meticulously restored 1930s-style replica of Sofiankatu street and several historic houses.

name: Old Market Hall (Vanha kauppahalli)
blurb: Old brick hall next to Market Square packed with gourmet food boutiques; hunt down the beaver-sausage stall.

name: Pronto Central Station
blurb: Compact Italian café-restaurant at Central Station; pizza al taglio and focaccia make a quick, cheap meal.

name: Lepakkomies
blurb: Two-floor Kallio pub with a basement venue; bar entry is free, but club nights carry an entrance fee.
priceText: Free entry to bar; club nights charge entry; beer from €4

name: Molly Malone's
blurb: Irish pub-nightclub by the Central Railway Station; live bands most nights, often covering English-language songs.

name: Kotiharju Sauna
blurb: Helsinki's last wood-fired public sauna, with separate men's and women's sides; cooling off outside in winter is a highlight.
priceText: Sauna 16 €; students (Finnish student card or ISIC), pensioners, unemployed and disabled 13 €; towel rent 4 €

name: Outdoor Icepark (central Helsinki)
blurb: Outdoor ice rink in central Helsinki; skate rental costs extra, and the café beside it serves hot glögi to warm up.

name: Estonian Open-Air Museum
blurb: 72 buildings of Estonian village life from the tsarist era, set in a dense forest; open through the winter.
priceText: Winter (29 Sep–22 Apr) single ticket 14 €; concession 10 € (conditions not stated)

name: Vabamu (Museum of Occupations and Freedom)
blurb: Museum prompting visitors to think about Estonia's recent past and the precariousness of freedom.

name: KUMU Art Museum
blurb: Estonia's national art museum in a huge 2006 building; its architecture alone is reason enough to visit.
when: Tue–Wed, Fri–Sun 10:00–18:00; Thu to 20:00; closed Mon

name: EKKM (Contemporary Art Museum of Estonia)
blurb: Free contemporary art museum that opens through a café and fills an old industrial building with changing shows.

name: Kohvik Narva
blurb: Old-style café with a Soviet-era feel; cheap solyanka, pelmeni, pancakes and cake, ordered at the counter.

name: Kuldse Notsu Kõrts
blurb: Old-school Estonian restaurant steps from the main square; house beer and pork knuckle with spicy mustard are the tips.

name: Teater
blurb: Underground club off Vabaduse square; music leans to 1990s and 2000s hits, the door is loose, and the crowd arrives around midnight.

name: Drink Baar
blurb: Pub with the largest beer range in town, including BrewDog and Mikkeller imports, and English-style pub grub.

name: Tallinn Botanic Garden
blurb: Botanic garden about 10 km out of town; its greenhouses offer warmth in winter and suit plant lovers.

name: Atlantis H2O Aquapark
blurb: Water park with wave and flow pools and eight slides (the longest tops 120 m); a toddler zone too.

name: House of the Blackheads (Melngalvju nams)
blurb: Riga merchants' guild house with upper ballrooms and a museum; part of the building is the tourist office.

name: St. Peter's Church
blurb: Riga's first church, dating from 1209; a lift climbs its tower for views across the city.
when: Tower lift not available on Mondays

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
blurb: The country's leading art collection, with many works by Latvian artists.

name: Triangula Bastion
blurb: Modern building that exposes a fragment of the old fortification wall; reputed to have Riga's finest viewing terraces.

name: Vermanitis
blurb: Budget Latvian restaurant in an 'authentic' setting in Riga's Centrs district: fried fish, half chicken and cheap beer.
priceText: Fried fish €3, salmon steak €5, half chicken €2.50, 500 ml beer €2.10

name: Alus Arsenals
blurb: Snug cellar restaurant by Riga Castle: meat and fish plates and well-made local beers.

name: Pūce
blurb: Club that draws a younger crowd: rock and pop upstairs, techno and alternative in the basement; busiest Thu–Sat.
priceText: Free entry + face control; beer €2–3, long drinks €4–6, cocktails €6–9

name: French Bar
blurb: Old, inexpensive and compact; students and foreigners favour it, and international sports are shown on TV.

name: Wolftrike Drift Hall
blurb: Indoor drift-driving hall, one of Riga's adrenaline-sport options for a group outing.

name: Riga Zoo
blurb: Small but fairly popular zoo on the Outer East Bank, with entry at about €4–6.

name: Gediminas Tower (Upper Castle)
blurb: Tower of the Upper Castle, the hilltop part of a 13th-century castle complex above the Old Town.

name: Gate of Dawn (Aušros vartai)
blurb: Last of Vilnius's medieval city gates still standing, crowned by a chapel with a big icon of the Virgin Mary.

name: Vilnius Cathedral
blurb: Cathedral rebuilt after repeated fires since 1251; its baroque St Casimir chapel is the highlight. Free to enter.

name: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights
blurb: Housed in a former KGB headquarters; the focus is the Lithuanian experience of Soviet occupation.

name: Halės turgus (Hale Market Hall)
blurb: The 1906 market hall that resembles a railway station, with food stalls and eateries on its eastern side.

name: Buga Sotu
blurb: Cheap traditional Lithuanian menu (dumplings, kibinai, carp), with live music on Fridays and sometimes Saturdays.

name: BIX
blurb: Rock band's own bar: live rock and metal on Friday nights, karaoke on Thursdays, and a dance floor.

name: Soho Club
blurb: LGBT club that gets very crowded, open on Friday and Saturday nights.

name: Lindy Hop Klubas
blurb: Lindy Hop swing-dance club with lessons and social nights; retro outfits are optional.

name: Akropolis ice rink
blurb: Shopping mall with an ice rink and a multiplex cinema; a simple indoor skate on a cold day.

name: European Solidarity Centre
blurb: Museum on Solidarity, the union that became Poland's communist-era opposition; the roof terrace viewpoint is free.

name: Gdańsk Crane (Żuraw)
blurb: The old medieval port crane on the Motława, a city landmark; in winter it is open Tuesday to Sunday.
priceText: 8 zł adults, 5 zł concession, 1 zł children

name: Westerplatte
blurb: Park at the site where WWII opened in September 1939, with info panels, bunkers and a monument; free.

name: St. Mary's Basilica, Gdańsk (Bazylika Mariacka)
blurb: Vast Gothic brick church with room for over 20,000 people and a large astronomical clock inside.

name: Montownia Foodhall
blurb: Food hall with roughly 18 eateries, mostly world cuisines, housed in a former U-boat assembly plant.

name: Pierogarnia Mandu Gdańsk Śródmieście
blurb: Pierogi (dumpling) spot with generous portions, so one per person is plenty; cheap and busy at lunch.

name: Loft
blurb: Late-night bar-club: no door fee, a young crowd, and free snacks late on weekends.
priceText: No entry charges; beer 6 zł, tatanka 8 zł

name: Pijalnia Wódki i Piwa
blurb: Vodka-and-beer bar in communist-era decor; shots are the norm and toasties are the bar snack.

name: Mariacka Street evening walk
blurb: Evening stroll down Mariacka Street, a contender for Europe's prettiest street.

name: Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre guided tour
blurb: Theatre offering guided tours in English and Polish; check the site for tour times.

name: Wawel Cathedral
blurb: Royal archcathedral on Wawel Hill; the ticket covers the royal tombs, Sigismund's Bell and two cathedral museums.
priceText: 26 zł adult; reduced 18 zł (students with ISIC, pupils, seniors, children)

name: St Mary's Basilica, Kraków (Bazylika Mariacka)
blurb: 14th-century brick Gothic basilica on the Main Square; a trumpet call rings out hourly from its uneven towers.
when: Mon–Sat 12:00–18:00; Sun 14:00–18:00; no visits during Mass

name: Princes Czartoryski Museum
blurb: Branch of the National Museum, refurbished and reopened in late 2019; it houses Leonardo's Lady with an Ermine.
priceText: Wikivoyage: adult 35 zł, concession 20 zł; Tuesday free

name: Remuh Synagogue
blurb: Synagogue in Kazimierz beside a historic Jewish cemetery that holds the grave of Moses Isserles.
when: Sun–Fri 09:00–18:00; closed Sat and Jewish holidays

name: Judah Food Market
blurb: Street-food market in Kazimierz with 11 trucks: zapiekanki, pierogi, chimney cakes, kumpir, burgers and tempura.

name: Zakąski i Wódka
blurb: Traditional Polish bar where you can eat well as well as drink: soups, pickles and bread, about 30 zł a person.

name: Alchemia
blurb: Iconic Kazimierz bar that defined the district's look; it sometimes hosts concerts and film screenings downstairs.

name: Ambasada Śledzia (Herring Embassy)
blurb: Old Town bar with a courtyard patio and verse scribbled across its walls; tapas at 4 zł a dish.
priceText: Polish tapas 4 zł a dish; drinks 6 zł

name: Park Wodny waterpark
blurb: Indoor waterpark with slides, a children's pool and a sauna; a good wet-weather option in December.

name: Benedictine Abbey in Tyniec
blurb: Benedictine abbey on the Vistula bank, once one of early Poland's key scholarly centres; a short trip out of town.
priceText: Guided abbey visit 6 zł; museum 7 zł normal, 5 zł reduced

name: Royal Castle (Zamek Królewski)
blurb: Royal castle in Warsaw's Old Town with several tour routes; the Royal Route is the main draw, open Tuesday to Sunday.
priceText: Royal Route with audio guide 60 zł (reduced 45 zł); special 1 zł without audio guide for EU/EFTA citizens aged 8–26 with birth-date proof
when: Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00 (last entry 16:00); closed Mon, 24, 25 and 31 Dec

name: Warsaw Rising Museum (Muzeum Powstania Warszawskiego)
blurb: Multimedia museum on the 1944 Warsaw Uprising, a must for most visitors; free admission on Thursdays.
priceText: Regular 35 zł; reduced 30 zł; free admission on Thursdays

name: Palace of Culture and Science observation deck
blurb: Warsaw's best-known skyscraper, built in the 1950s as a supposed Stalin 'gift'; its observation deck gives city views.

name: Królikarnia
blurb: Mokotów palace and park whose name nods to a fake rabbit warren; park and museum are both free.
priceText: Free entrance to the park and the museum

name: Prasowy
blurb: Revamped milk bar near Plac Unii: homely, budget cooking given a creative, arts-friendly spin.

name: Zapiecek
blurb: Chain serving pierogi and Polish soups, mostly in the Old and New Town; the menu rarely changes and prices are low.

name: Club 70
blurb: Club spinning 1970s and 1980s hits with a relaxed door and a fun crowd; drinks are on the pricey side.
priceText: Entry free to about 20 zł; 0.5 L beer 10 zł

name: Przekąski Zakąski
blurb: Cult 24/7 bar with 4 zł drinks, currently in a temporary tent in the centre after moving.

name: Alternative Warsaw walking tour
blurb: Two-hour walking tour of Praga covering its history and Warsaw's wider story; pay what you want.

name: Tor Stegny ice rink
blurb: Outdoor ice rink in Warsaw's south that opens only once the temperature drops below 10°C.
when: Open when the temperature is below 10°C
